6.1.rationale: The cited emergency/conflict/disaster provisions and related protection measures are explicitly framed as “Special Protection for Children in Emergency Situations” and list only child categories (including child refugees, children in riots/natural disasters/armed conflict). The passages do not identify women or girls in these situations as a group requiring special protection, nor do they establish women-specific emergency/disaster/conflict protection measures.

6.2.rationale: The policy explicitly includes “Human trafficking” as a form of violence, provides for a task force on trafficking in persons, and cites the national anti-trafficking law in its legal basis—each of which is sufficient to include trafficking victims (including women) within scope under the coding rules.

6.3.rationale: The passages mention partnerships with the business sector to provide employment opportunity information and training for women/children victims of violence, and mention creating a “friendly and safe work environment atmosphere for women,” but they do not explicitly identify women workers/employees as a specific protected target group or provide workplace-specific protection measures against violence/exploitation for women workers as such.

6.4.rationale: None of the cited sentences mention elderly women or provide any protection measures specifically targeted at elderly women; the provisions are general to women and children victims of violence or to children’s special protection categories.

6.5.rationale: Disability is only referenced in the context of children (e.g., “Children with Disabilities” and accessibility for children with disabilities). The coding rules exclude counting disability protections that are solely within child protection, and there is no explicit identification of women with disabilities or people with disabilities (generally) as beneficiaries of special protection/services in the provided sentences.

6.6.rationale: The cited sentences do not mention women heads of household/families or provide any special protection measures targeted to them. References to families/parents’ obligations and general women/children protection do not constitute targeted measures for women-headed households.

6.7.rationale: Minority/isolated groups are mentioned only for children (“Special Protection for Children from Minority and Isolated Groups”). There is no explicit mention of women from minority or isolated groups as a target group for special protection or services in the provided sentences.

6.8.rationale: The only explicit “in conflict with the law” provisions concern children in conflict with the law. Other legal aid/judicial assistance provisions are framed around victims of violence, which the coding rules say should not be inferred to cover women as suspects/defendants/perpetrators/witnesses in conflict with the law.

6.9.rationale: The cited sentences address minority and isolated groups only in relation to children and do not explicitly identify Indigenous peoples/customary communities/masyarakat adat (or Indigenous women) as beneficiaries of special protection measures or services.

6.10.rationale: The policy explicitly provides “Special Protection for Children in Emergency Situations” to “Children who become refugees,” which constitutes a special protection measure targeted at refugees/forced displacement (even though limited to children).

6.11.rationale: None of the cited sentences mention domestic workers or provide any special protection measures targeted at domestic workers; references to domestic violence are not the same as protections for domestic workers as an employment group.

6.12.rationale: The cited sentences provide for temporary shelter/safe houses for victims of violence generally, but do not identify women experiencing homelessness as a specific target group or provide homelessness-specific protection measures.

6.13.rationale: The only incarceration-related reference is to “Children of female convicts/detainees” within children’s emergency special protection. There are no provisions targeting women who are former inmates/formerly incarcerated women themselves.
